text:
incident-bot: Alert: KV prefix hit-rate collapse detected for customer auryn in eu-west-1 dedicated pool. severity: P1. Error spike and token-latency increase since 08:23 UTC. Auto-escalating to on-call.

pagerduty-bot: Paging elena (oncall) — incident assigned. Please acknowledge. :rotating_light:

elena: acked. joining. seeing the alert in console — top-line: per-prefix hitrate for auryn/_user/ dropped from ~82% to <4%. Errors correlate with 504s and 500s from the edge.

auryn-ops: We started seeing higher 500s on our end ~08:22, latency spiked. Confirming traffic unchanged. Appreciate quick help.

miguel: I’m on KV cache stack. First guess is cache pollution or a prefetch job gone wild for that tenant prefix. pulling prefix metrics now.

andy: adding context — auryn is on a dedicated pool with shared KV nodes (per-pool, multi-tenant prefixes). We recently rolled a prefetch change in the pool yesterday night. Could be related.

incident-bot: Runbook excerpt for KV hit-rate collapse: 1) Verify prefix distribution 2) Check prefetch/policy churn 3) Validate cache config (enabled/disabled, TTLs) 4) If noisy tenant, isolate using per-tenant ring or throttle prefetch 5) Hotfix: disable pool prefetch or apply strict prefix filters.

miguel: checked metrics:
```
prefix=auryn/_user/ hit_rate=3.7% window=5m
prefetch_write_rate=120req/s
cache_evictions/sec=450
backend_miss_latency=75ms
```
Most of the traffic is cold misses with high eviction pressure. Looks like prefetch spiked.

sasha: I’m tailing the prefetch scheduler logs. There's a job for auryn that queued 20k keys at 08:20 due to a mis-ordered prefix pattern in the new matcher. patch reverted but damage done.

elena: immediate mitigation — disable pool-level prefetch for auryn and pin aura's prefixes to per-tenant namespace to avoid pollution. miguel, can you run the disable? I'll coordinate customer comms.

miguel: running disable now. Command:
```
POST /internal/prefetch/disable
payload: {"pool":"dedicated-eu-west-1-auryn","reason":"hit-rate collapse - emergency"}
```
Response: 202 accepted. prefetched-job queue drained.

andy: routing change in progress: diverting auryn traffic to fallback per-tenant cache ring to stop writes into shared pool. Applying policy patch.

auryn-ops: Noted improvement on our side — error rate dropping, tail latency improving. Thanks.

miguel: monitoring — hit rate recovered to ~47% in 2m after draining, evictions down to 12/sec. Still below baseline; working to warm prefixes. Will kick a targeted warm-up for their top 200 keys.

elena: warming script queued. warming command (internal):
```
python tools/warm_prefix.py --tenant auryn --pool dedicated-eu-west-1 --top 200
```
Kick off now.

miguel: warm-up started. will follow until hit-rate stabilizes. also working a longer-term fix: tighten prefix matcher and add per-tenant quota for prefetch jobs to prevent runaway.

sasha: filing a post-deploy rollback note re: yesterday's matcher change. tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for code review.

elena: handoff in 15. miguel will take next shift. auryn-ops — any residual customer impact?

auryn-ops: We're back to normal for now. We'll keep monitoring on our side and report any regressions. Appreciate the quick response.

miguel: will stay on for the handoff. follow-up actions: 1) revert matcher ship permanently 2) add per-tenant prefetch cap 3) create alert for prefetch queue spikes 4) run a small canary of matcher fix in staging.

elena: adding to incident doc and will run brief postmortem. tagging eng-sre for follow-up. Closing active paging but keeping thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
